fields.name: post_button_target
fields.description: During the video cycle, read the goal's temporal relation and locate the hand's downward press on the gray button on its white base. For 'right before', select the instructed-color cube's last released target placement before the press; for 'right after', select its first released target placement after the press. Ignore subsequent off-target reset placements. Save the earliest shown frame of the selected placement with a visible gap between the released cube and the withdrawing hand. Inspect the rest of the video and track that ring itself, not just the release location. If it remains stationary, store only the release frame label. If it moves, store an ordered list beginning with the release frame, followed for each subsequent shuffle affecting that ring by the last stationary frame before the shuffle, every shown frame during the shuffle, and the first frame establishing its settled location. Keep labels in chronological order and omit duplicates. At every act cycle copy the incoming value unchanged. e.g. "V192" or ["V512", "V704", "V720", "V736", "V752", "V768"]
fields.annotation: At the video cycle, select the instructed cube's target placement according to the goal's temporal relation to the demonstrated button press: its last released target placement before the press for 'right before', or its first released target placement after the press for 'right after'. Ignore subsequent off-target reset placements. Record the earliest shown frame of the selected placement with a visible gap between the released cube and the withdrawing hand. Track the selected ring itself through the rest of the demonstration. If it remains stationary, store only that release frame label. If it moves, store an ordered list beginning with the release frame, followed for each subsequent shuffle affecting that ring by the last stationary frame before the shuffle, every shown frame during the shuffle, and the first frame establishing its settled location. Keep labels in chronological order and omit duplicates. Carry the value unchanged through all act cycles. e.g. "V192" or ["V512", "V704", "V720", "V736", "V752", "V768"]

action:
At the video cycle output memory only. Execution begins with an open hand above the table and the instructed-color cube at its reset position. The instruction refers to a temporal relationship in the demonstration: place the cube on the target selected by the goal's 'right before' or 'right after' relation to the demonstrated button press, as recorded in post_button_target. Do not press the button in execution, replay other demonstrated placements, or wait for a new button event.

Use post_button_target to identify the purple ring underneath the released instructed-color cube in the saved frame, or the first frame if the value is a list. For a list, follow that same ring through the saved shuffle frames to its final settled position; its release-time position is not necessarily its final position. Match the ring's final position to the current scene using the button and final ring layout. This is the destination, even if another ring is closer to the cube. Ignore cubes of other colors.

Estimate world positions using calibrated camera rays. Intersect ring-center rays with the tabletop plane z=0. Identify the cube's top-face corners carefully, using the current wrist image when clear. Back-project the corners onto the approximately z=0.04 top-face plane and take their geometric center in world coordinates; do not use an approximate colored-region center or the cube's silhouette center. For a pixel [u,v] and its camera's supplied world-to-camera calibration, use C=-R^T t, d=R^T K^-1[u,v,1], and X=C+((0.04-C_z)/d_z)d. Use the resulting horizontal cube center for both the z=0.15 pickup approach and the z=0.02 grasp. Check the top-face boundaries and use both calibrated camera views when needed, aiming for horizontal localization error comfortably below 0.01 m. The 0.02 m approach arrival tolerance recognizes an already reached approach despite motion error; it does not permit that much error in the commanded cube-center estimate. Transform two points along a top-face edge into world coordinates on that plane before deriving grasp yaw; an image-plane edge angle is not world yaw. Compute the edge's horizontal world angle with atan2(delta_y, delta_x), then choose its square-equivalent yaw modulo pi/2 in [-pi/4, pi/4), the representative nearest zero. Orient the hand straight down, roll approximately pi and pitch zero, with this canonical yaw; maintain that orientation throughout pickup, carrying, and release.

Apply these observable-state rules: If the hand is open, the cube is not already on the remembered destination, and the hand is not at its pickup approach, move above the cube center to z=0.15 with gripper open. If the open hand is at this approach (allowing normal endpoint error), descend to the cube center at z=0.02 and close. If the cube is grasped and the hand is low at pickup, lift vertically to z=0.15 with gripper closed. If holding the cube at clearance height but not above the destination, move horizontally to the destination center at z=0.15 with gripper closed. If holding the cube above the destination at clearance height, descend at that destination center to commanded z=0.005 and open. If the hand is open and low over the cube released onto the destination, retract vertically to z=0.15 with gripper open. Do not mistake a recently released cube for a fresh pickup; its position on the remembered destination and the open fingers establish the retreat condition. Do not insist that the measured release height equal 0.005: contact can leave the TCP around 0.01–0.02.

Use approximate arrival tolerances of 0.02 m at approach height and 0.01 m horizontally above the destination, refining the actual destination from the visible ring rather than substituting the imperfect reached TCP position. Preserve closed fingers throughout lift and transport. Never issue an identical-pose waypoint merely to change the gripper; include at least 0.002 m of movement.

For an unrecognized or ambiguous state, use the visible grasp and geometry to recover: lift a securely held cube to clearance before lateral movement; with an empty hand, move open to a clear elevated observation pose and relocalize the instructed cube and remembered ring. Do not choose a different target because the intended one is occluded. If the cube is already correctly placed, withdraw without disturbing it.
